description: REQ-002 ('WHEN the harness explores a new generation THE SYSTEM SHALL mutate 1-2 of the four NUMERIC knobs...') is unimplemented as an actual system behavior. mutate() in sol-genome.mjs is a correct, fully-tested pure function (PROP-002/PROP-003 all pass on inspection) -- but it is NEVER invoked anywhere in the production wiring. sol-gate-cli.mjs (the ONLY entrypoint sol-trade/run.sh calls) imports only {loadGenome, genomeId} from sol-genome.mjs (sol-gate-cli.mjs:16) -- it never imports or calls mutate(). Grepping the entire worktree for `mutate(` outside test files returns zero matches. Consequently every pass loads the SAME genome (SAFE_DEFAULT_GENOME merged with an override file that nothing in this codebase ever writes), so genomeId(genome) is identical on every pass, forever. The feature's own spec Provenance section explicitly names `shouldMutateThisPass` (genome.mjs's cadence-based exploration trigger, the exact PM mechanism that decides WHEN to call mutate() each pass and is called from polymarket-trade/run.sh every pass via `node genome.mjs --maybe-mutate`) as an artifact this spec 'structurally mirrors' and must copy+tweak -- behavioral-spec.md line 13: '...loadGenome / mutate / genomeId / toExportLines / shouldMutateThisPass'. Neither shouldMutateThisPass nor any cadence/exploration-trigger equivalent exists in sol-genome.mjs or sol-gate-cli.mjs. This is not a minor omission: because no mutant genome is ever explored, no genome_id other than the single static baseline id will ever appear in sol-trade.trace.jsonl's genome-linkage lines, which means REQ-012b/013/014's entire downstream attribution+summarization+promotion pipeline (independently correct and well-tested, see FIND-002) can NEVER have a mutantId to evaluate in production. The feature is named 'franklin-sol-evolvable-edge' and REQ-002/012b/013/014/015 collectively promise an evolving, earnings-gated exploration loop; as wired, the genome is permanently frozen at baseline and nothing evolves.
